verdict.reasoning: Rendered PDF page 819 (printed 797) at 300 dpi shows Figure E.10 as a flowchart: Evaluate condition-1 -> 'Condition-1 true' rounded decision; its 'yes' exits right to a vertical line that also collects the 'yes' exits of 'Condition-2 true' and 'Condition-n true' and ends in an arrow to 'Truth value is true'; each 'no' goes down to the next Evaluate box, and the 'no' of 'Condition-n true' arrows to 'Truth value is false'. The markdown (page-819.md) keeps every text label in order but no edges: the 'yes' labels are fused into the decision text ('Condition-1 yes / true'), and the two terminals are a two-column table with no statement of which path reaches which. The fact that any 'yes' ends evaluation with a true result (the short-circuit the figure exists to show) is not recoverable from the markdown except by inference from the caption. The claim quotes both sources accurately. It is a genuine content loss, but in the informative Annex E, so it has no normative effect.
